exposure: Adolescent motherhood (age <20 years at first birth)
cohort: Adolescent primigravidae completing 28 weeks of gestation with singleton pregnancy, compared to primigravidae aged 20-25 years, at a tertiary care teaching hospital in North-East India
finding: Adolescent mothers had a higher incidence of pre-eclampsia and preterm deliveries, and their infants had a higher incidence of low birth weight and neonatal intensive care unit admission.
mod_finding: There was no significant difference in mode of delivery between adolescent and older mothers.
